q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Net ROAS rose ~31% while net profit did not fall — it actually improved from a large loss to near-breakeven; the apparent mismatch comes from much lower ad spend improving ROAS while sales and contribution also fell. 

- Key numbers: Net ROAS 0.97 (2026-09-15..2026-10-13) vs 0.74 prior (+31%); Net profit INR -28,492 vs INR -532,557 prior (improved by INR 504,065).  
- Why ROAS rose: Ad spend (P&L basis) fell 52% — INR 2,069,132 → INR 1,002,453 — which raises ROAS arithmetic even though sales fell.  
- Why profit stayed poor (and only moved from large loss to small loss): Contribution margin fell 37% — INR 1,536,575 → INR 973,961 — and net sales fell ~38%; the drop in gross contribution offsets much of the benefit from lower ad spend, leaving net profit only slightly negative.  
- What else moved: Orders -41% (1,644 → 965), clicks -55% and impressions -48% (lower volume), while cost-per-order and CAC improved modestly — so efficiency rose but volume and margin contracted.

Worth checking: did we intentionally cut ad budgets or pause campaigns (major ad spend decline concentrated on Meta and Google)? If yes, confirm which campaigns to restore or re-run a channel/campaign drill to see where the margin loss concentrated.

Period: 2026-09-15..2026-10-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14
